notes: Research. Origin: the issue tree (logic tree, diagnostic tree) is the McKinsey problem-solving staple, formalised in Barbara Minto's Pyramid Principle (the same MECE grouping read top-down as a question rather than as an assertion), popularised in Ethan Rasiel's The McKinsey Way (1999) and given its modern textbook treatment in Conn and McLean, Bulletproof Problem Solving (2018). Two structures share one diagram. An ISSUE TREE decomposes a root question into mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive sub-questions and stops there; it is a map of what you would have to know. A HYPOTHESIS TREE goes one step further: each branch carries a candidate answer stated so that it could be wrong, plus the analysis that would show it wrong. Hypothesis-driven problem solving (the 'day one answer', the ghost pack) exists to stop the boil-the-ocean data gathering an issue tree alone invites: you do not collect everything, you collect the one observation that kills the most branches. What each slot forces: question forces a single decision-relevant question rather than a topic; issue forces siblings that are MECE, so that no cause hides between branches and no branch is counted twice; hypothesis forces a falsifiable sentence with a direction and a magnitude, not a subject heading; test forces the disconfirming observation, named in advance, with the threshold that would settle it; evidence forces the observation actually in hand, kept separate from the reading of it. Common misuse: hypotheses too vague to be wrong ('marketing is weak'); confirmation-seeking tests that look for supporting data instead of the killer; overlapping or incomplete siblings; the tree used as a work plan (tasks) rather than a logic structure (claims); deep trees that never reach an observation; and prioritising by ease of analysis rather than by which branch, if resolved, most moves the answer. Design consequence for provenance: the test slot is almost always derived, because sources volunteer explanations and almost never volunteer the observation that would kill their own explanation. That contrast is this framework's provenance story: with derived hidden the page shows a question and a heap of volunteered hypotheses with no tests under any of them (a wish list); with derived shown, the MECE issue scaffolding appears above them, the unstated sibling hypotheses appear beside them, and a test hangs under every hypothesis. Scout: launched with Part B plus a framework-specific addendum (what a live diagnostic question looks like, the demand for three or more volunteered candidate answers, quantitative observations that cut both ways, and an explicit warning off two-sided theses and single-chain root-cause narratives, which sibling frameworks own; also excluded the nine episode dates already claimed by sibling agents). It returned three ranked candidates. Chose #1, the 2025-08-09 weekly recap, because the hosts pose the diagnostic question in one sentence out loud, announce that several explanations exist, then volunteer five of them in one continuous segment, each with its own stated connective back to the question, and because the segment contains the rare thing this framework needs: one stated falsification condition. Rejected #2 (2025-09-08 Census AI adoption: excellent contradictory evidence but the root question is mangled in the transcript and the explanations are spread across two distant segments) and #3 (2025-12-10 venture fundraising: strong question, but the candidate answers are mostly speculative futures rather than explanations of the stated anomaly). Design decisions. (1) Kept all five registry slot ids and all four registry relations. Refined two slot descriptions: `hypothesis` typical_provenance is set to 'either' rather than 'derived', because the whole provenance story of this framework is that sources volunteer hypotheses freely (five fact hypotheses in the TBPN example, two in the classic) and never volunteer the test; and `bears_on` is described as running from an observation to a hypothesis or to the question the observation makes a puzzle, so the anomaly evidence can attach to the root. (2) The provenance contrast is deliberately built around the `test` slot: 12 of the 12 tests across both examples are derived except one (t_oai in the TBPN example, quoted verbatim), so hiding the derived layer leaves a question, the volunteered explanations connected by the speakers' own connectives, the evidence, and no way to tell any explanation from any other. That is the wish list the framework exists to replace. (3) The issue layer is entirely derived in both examples and is inserted between the question and the volunteered hypotheses, so the full view shows the MECE scaffolding the source never built. The four TBPN issues are MECE by construction on a ratio: the measurement misassigns work, the numerator genuinely rose, the denominator is capped by supply, the denominator is capped by demand. The demand branch is empty in the source, which is the sharpest single observation the tree produces. (4) idea_bearing_slot is `hypothesis`, with ideas on the two derived hypotheses h_blind (nobody can measure AI revenue) and h_pilot (enterprise AI stuck before production). (5) The classic case is a synthetic profitability diagnostic in the standard consulting form, written so the two volunteered explanations arrive without tests and the source states, in its last sentence, that nobody proposed a way to tell them apart. validate: 0 errors, 0 warnings on the first run.
